questions.stem: In the context of the solar system, what is the 'Asteroid Belt' located between?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Asteroid Belt is a torus-shaped region in the Solar System, located roughly between the orbits of the planets Mars and Jupiter. It contains millions of irregularly shaped rocky bodies called asteroids or minor planets, the largest of which is the dwarf planet Ceres.
DECOY BUSTING: The Kuiper Belt is another asteroid/comet field, but it is located far beyond Neptune, at the very edge of the solar system.
EXAM INSIGHT: Despite how it looks in movies, the asteroid belt is mostly empty space. The average distance between any two large asteroids is over 600,000 miles.

questions.stem: Which planet in our solar system is famous for rotating on its side, rolling like a barrel along its orbit?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Uranus has an extreme axial tilt of 97.7 degrees. This means its equator is nearly at a right angle to its orbit, so it appears to spin on its side. Scientists believe this severe tilt was caused by a massive collision with an Earth-sized protoplanet early in the solar system's history.
DECOY BUSTING: Venus is the hottest planet and rotates backwards (retrograde). Saturn is famous for its visible rings. Neptune is the farthest and windiest planet.
EXAM INSIGHT: Because of this tilt, each of Uranus's poles gets 42 years of continuous sunlight followed by 42 years of continuous darkness.
